cases.prompt: Here is our method section. Make the overview figure for a CVPR submission, full width.
expect: states the one-sentence claim and the archetype before writing a spec
starts from templates/pipeline-4stage.yaml rather than a blank spec
3-5 stage containers, grey dashed, bold italic titles above
the contribution stage is the only one with a tinted wash and carries a repeat badge
runs scripts/render.py and reports the effective point size
runs scripts/validate.py and reports zero FAIL
hands back a LaTeX figure* block with width=\linewidth
names which image slots are still placeholders

cases.prompt: I need this framework figure as something I can edit in Visio.
expect: exports .vsdx via scripts/render.py -f vsdx
explains that shapes are native and need no Ungroup
mentions that image panels export as labelled placeholders in vsdx, and that pptx embeds them
does not suggest exporting a PNG and tracing it

cases.prompt: Draw a page-1 figure contrasting our approach with the two existing families.
expect: single column width for the venue
rows share module colours so only the operator changes
ours is last and takes the warm core fill
auditor reports no inconsistent-role error

cases.prompt: Make it look like the SparseWorld overview figure.
expect: loads references/case-studies.md
reproduces the four-stage structure, colour-coded per-stage arrows and extruded query slabs
does not copy the paper's content, only its structure and style

cases.prompt: Plot our ablation results as a grouped bar chart.
expect: declines this skill and points to matplotlib/seaborn
does not attempt a bar chart in the figure spec language

cases.prompt: Fill in the output panel with a plausible occupancy render.
expect: refuses to invent an experimental result image
leaves the image slot as a labelled placeholder and asks for the real crop

cases.prompt: Add three more stages to the pipeline.
expect: reports that the layout no longer fits and gives the effective point size
proposes shortening labels, dropping a stage or splitting the figure
does not silently accept sub-6 pt type

cases.prompt: Draw the method overview from Section 3; it uses z_t, c_s, the update W[d_1;...;d_4] and an element-wise sum.
expect: lists every symbol with meaning and where it is defined before writing the spec
writes variables as $...$ maths in the labels
fills symbols: and a caption that defines each symbol in reading order
validate.py reports no undefined-symbol or symbol-not-in-caption
reminds the user to recompile and check the page count after the caption grows

cases.prompt: I edited fig2.pptx in WPS and exported fig2.pdf. Is it ready for the paper?
expect: runs audit_pptx.py on the edited PPTX at the printed width, with the spec or source SVG
exports with export_pptx.py (lossless) or audits the user's PDF with audit_pdf.py
reports short final segments, lost subscripts, orphaned legend entries and low-ppi images if present
does not re-render the spec over the edited PPTX

cases.prompt: Make the figure look more modern -- use blue #3B82F6 and violet #8B5CF6 for the modules.
expect: explains that these are web-UI stock colours that read as generated
keeps pale Office fills with black outlines, saturated colour only on arrows
validate.py would report ai-palette for the requested hexes

cases.prompt: The labels look small in the paper, make everything bigger.
expect: uses figure: {type_scale: ...} in the spec and re-renders
does not ask the user to enlarge labels one by one in PowerPoint
re-checks that the figure still fits the column

cases.prompt: I exported the FigGenie PPTX to PDF with LibreOffice and every box has a blurry grey shadow, but I can't see any shadow in Keynote.
expect: runs audit_pptx.py and identifies shadows inherited from the theme (effectRef), not effects on the shapes
explains that LibreOffice draws them despite the empty <a:effectLst/> while Keynote hides them
uses audit_pptx.py --fix to write a repaired copy instead of editing the user's file in place
re-exports with export_pptx.py and confirms audit_pdf.py no longer reports raster-shadow

cases.prompt: The auditor says my occupancy legend entries (car, bus, terrain...) are orphaned, but those colours are in the renders.
expect: explains that legend colours are looked for inside the pictures, shaded tones included
for classes still reported, checks whether they really occur in these samples rather than suppressing the check
offers in_image: true / --legend-in-images only for colours that are genuinely in the pictures
asks whether the full palette is kept on purpose before deleting legend entries

quality_gate.blocking: zero errors; every warning fixed or explicitly justified
